claim: Álzaga and Lauret (2024/2025) prove vol(S^d)/8 is the highest volume of a pair of d-dimensional isospectral non-isometric SPHERICAL orbifolds for d>=5, an extremal-volume result in the same spherical isospectrality family as Bari-Hunsicker but not a heat-coefficient counting result.
stance_target: whether this is a competitor to the manuscript's hyperbolic cone-orbifold priority claim
quoted_support: We prove that vol(S^{d})/8 is the highest volume of a pair of d-dimensional isospectral and non-isometric spherical orbifolds for any d\geq5.

claim: The paper additionally proves vol(S^{2n-1})/11 is the highest volume of a pair of (2n-1)-dimensional isospectral non-isometric spherical SPACE FORMS under specific congruence conditions on n modulo 5.
stance_target: precise scope of the extremal-volume result
scope_conditions: (2n-1)-dimensional spherical space forms; n>=11 and n=1 mod 5, or n>=7 and n=2 mod 5, or n>=3 and n=3 mod 5
quoted_support: Furthermore, we show that vol(S^{2n-1})/11 is the highest volume of a pair of (2n-1)-dimensional isospectral and non-isometric spherical space forms if either n\geq11 and n\equiv 1\pmod 5, or n\geq7 and n\equiv 2\pmod 5, or n\geq3 and n\equiv 3\pmod 5.

claim: This paper was accepted in Revista de la Union Matematica Argentina (February 2025), post-dating and extending the spherical-orbifold isospectrality literature that includes Bari-Hunsicker, but remains entirely in constant positive curvature with no heat-trace coefficient analysis.
stance_target: publication venue and continuity of the spherical isospectrality research program
quoted_support: Accepted in Revista de la Unión Matemática Argentina (February 2025)
entities: Revista de la Unión Matemática Argentina
